# FINDINGS.md — Phase 1 static sweep

Flat, sortable. One line per finding. No fixes; no per-finding editorializing.

## Methodology & coverage (read before trusting a count)

- **cppcheck 2.7.4** `--enable=all -D__aarch64__ -D__HAIKU__`, whole `src/` tree (13,663 TUs). The arch define is load-bearing: without it `HaikuConfig.h:87 #error Unsupported architecture!` made cppcheck skip files as `noValidConfiguration`. With it, 0 files skipped, 0 `toomanyconfigs`.
- **clang-tidy 15.0.7** (`clang-analyzer-*,bugprone-*,cert-*,misc-*,performance-*` + `-Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion` as compiler args) on the **active surface only** (arm64 kernel, ENA, network stack, BFS, app_server remote). Full-tree clang-tidy needs a per-TU compile DB from the Jam cross-build, which is not provisioned here.
- **clang `-Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion` full build: DEFERRED.** It requires the Jam + `buildtools` aarch64-haiku cross-build (not present). Its intent is partially covered by clang-tidy's `clang-diagnostic-*` on the active surface and cppcheck's shadow/const checks.
- Duplicate reports of one header/template defect (reported once per includer) are collapsed to a single row.
- **`clang-diagnostic-error` rows dropped**: they are fatal parse failures (missing kernel headers/defines), not defects.

### Known false-positive-prone ids (confirm manually in Phase 4, per the flow)
- cppcheck `unknownMacro` (250), `syntaxError` (24), `preprocessorErrorDirective` (22), `internalAstError` (7) = cppcheck's own parser limits, **not bugs**. The 2 ENA "high" rows are `internalAstError` in vendored `ena-com/` — instrument noise.
- `nullPointerRedundantCheck` often means a benign check-after-use ordering, not a live NPD.

# Phase 2 — Known upstream issue cross-reference

**Source of truth:** Trac dumps the maintainer pulled from dev.haiku-os.org (bot-walled from the
build host): `query.csv` = component **File Systems/BFS**, all open (24 tickets); `query(1).csv` /
`query.rss` = a broad general/misc set (100 tickets). All matched tickets below are **open**
(`new`/`assigned`/`reopened`).

**Coverage gap (honest):** the **network-stack**, **app_server-remote**, and **kernel/arm64**
components were *not* dumped, so those Phase-1 clusters (radix.c uninitvar/null, arp.cpp null,
ipv4/ipv6 address checks, TCPEndpoint, StreamingRingBuffer) remain **un-cross-referenced**. Pull
`component=Network & Internet/*`, `Servers/app_server`, and `System/Kernel` to close it.

## Matches (static finding ↔ open Trac ticket)

| Phase-1 finding cluster | Trac | Ticket summary | Conf. | Why it matches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bfs/BPlusTree.cpp` — narrowing/implicit-widening in size math (`:134`, `:701`), assignment-in-if (`:577` +8) | [#14180](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/14180) | KDL on corrupt BFS — B+tree header size doesn't fit | **high** | A B+tree *header-size* KDL is exactly the failure a truncating size conversion in BPlusTree size math produces on hostile input. |
| `bfs/BPlusTree.cpp` — same cluster | [#11399](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/11399) | [BFS] Panic in BPlusTree::Find() | **high** | Our static hits are *in* the file that panics; Find() walks the same size/offset math. |
| `bfs/Inode.cpp` — narrowing (`:18`), assignment-in-if (`:4`), suspicious-string-compare | [#1242](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/1242) | Inode::WriteAttribute() incorrect for small_data items | **med** | Both point at Inode small_data/attribute handling. |
| `bfs/kernel_interface.cpp` — branch-clone (`:4`), narrowing | [#9449](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/9449) | bfs: SegFault while unmounting at shutdown | **med** | Unmount path lives here; relevant to DeBeOS forced-stop / crash-safety work. |
| `bfs/BlockAllocator.cpp` — narrowing in block math | [#20230](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/20230) | PANIC get_cached_block: invalid block number -858993457 | **med** | The negative block no. (`0xCCCCCCCC`) is a classic sign/width bug in block-number math. |
| BFS reliability (whole subsystem; ties to DeBeOS page-writer flush fix `8331882470`) | [#10765](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/10765), [#12676](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/12676), [#16830](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/16830) | volume-wide data corruption / corruption after hours / "be more robust on corrupted disks" | **med** | Long-standing corruption reports in the exact subsystem DeBeOS is hardening; corroborates the reliability priority, not a single line. |
| BFS consistency tooling | [#14456](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/14456), [#13414](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/13414), [#15609](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/15609), [#12698](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/12698) | KDL/failures in checkfs; checkfs misses errors | low | Context for Stage-4 crash-safety; not tied to a specific static hit. |
| VFS/storage (DeBeOS storage-perf + page-writer work) | [#14479](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/14479) | PANIC: vfs_read_pages() failed: Device timeout! | low | Same read/write-page path DeBeOS instrumented; general dump. |
| kernel VM robustness | [#14376](https://dev.haiku-os.org/ticket/14376) | Heap corruption after AreaTest is run | low | Kernel VM; general dump, not an active-surface static hit. |

**Not matched (checked, no ticket in the available dumps):** the ENA driver (DeBeOS-specific AWS
port — upstream Haiku has no ENA, confirmed by absence), and every network-stack / app_server-remote
/ arm64 cluster (components not dumped — see coverage gap above).

**High-confidence real (static hit ⋂ open long-standing report):** `BPlusTree.cpp` (#14180, #11399).
These jump to the top of the Phase-3 priority list.
